# Upgrading from 0.1

Carve 0.2 is a source break, and it is still a development version. A 0.1 document can parse in 0.2 without an error and still render different HTML, so anyone who keeps 0.1 files has to act: authors run `carve upgrade` on each file, and hosts review their render options and stored trees. The tool rewrites what has one safe 0.2 spelling, checks each rewrite against the 0.1 HTML, and reports the rest for a person to review.

The largest changes:

- A block marker directly under a paragraph line no longer starts a block; insert a blank line ([paragraphs](#paragraphs)).
- `---` and `___` breaks, `~~~` fences, `+` continuation lines, bare `_`, `~` and `=` pairs, and GFM separator rows lose their 0.1 meanings ([breaks](#breaks), [lists](#lists), [inline marks](#inline), [tables](#tables)).
- Raw HTML is escaped unless the host turns on `rawHtml` ([raw HTML](#html)).
- Stored trees move to AST 2.0 ([AST](#ast)).

## Run the rewrite tool {#tool}

Start with a copy of each 0.1 `.crv` file. Build `carve-js` on `main` with `npm ci` and `npm run build`. Its CLI is `node dist/cli.js` (installed as `carve`). In a working copy of a 0.1 document:

```sh
node dist/cli.js upgrade --check page.crv
node dist/cli.js upgrade --json page.crv
node dist/cli.js upgrade --write page.crv
node dist/cli.js fmt --write page.crv
```

`--check` writes nothing and exits 1 when a change or human review is needed. `--json` writes a structured report. Without `--write`, upgraded source goes to standard output and the report to standard error. `--write` replaces the input after checking the old and proposed HTML. A usage error exits 2. `--force` does not bypass an HTML mismatch. Run the tool **once per 0.1 file**: it is not idempotent on already upgraded source. This `upgrade` command is specific to the JavaScript reference engine; the shared [0.2 tooling contract](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/tooling.md#scope) does not require it.

Read the `rewrite`, `escape`, `report`, `upgrade-conflict` and `upgrade-mismatch` records. A mismatch prevents writing. Even a passing rewrite needs review: the tool's HTML comparison normalizes attribute order, whitespace between tags, and a leading line feed in list item text. Then compare representative pages rendered by both engines: headings and generated ids, list tightness and task items, table headers, footnotes, links, captions and raw HTML. The 0.2 output contract is [HTML](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/html.md). Markdown, plain text and ANSI output come from export renderers (`carve render --to markdown`, `--to plain`, `--to ansi`); their output is engine behavior, not part of the specification (C2-T-003). Keep the JSON upgrade report with the source change for review.

## Reading this page {#reading}

Each section below opens with what 0.2 changed for one construct and why, then lists every row of the [upgrade map](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/data/upgrade-map.json) for that construct. The row id links to its detail in the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md), which stays the normative record.

- The left block is the 0.1 source. The right block is the 0.2 source the tool writes, as `carve fmt` writes it in turn (`crv`). Where the tool proposes no source, the right block shows what 0.2 makes of the unchanged 0.1 source (`html`, or a description in `text`).
- <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> the tool changes the spelling. <Badge type="warning" text="escape" /> it escapes text that 0.2 would read as syntax. <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> a person has to decide. <Badge type="info" text="none" /> no source edit is needed.
- <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> the unchanged 0.1 source still parses in 0.2 but renders different HTML. Review these rows even when a document has no syntax error.
- An invisible character in a sample, such as a tab-like control character or a no-break space, is shown as its code point, for example `⟨U+00A0⟩`. A tab is a real tab.

## Paragraphs and continuation {#paragraphs}

In 0.1 every block kind had its own answer to whether it could interrupt a paragraph, so a wrapped line that only looked like a heading or quote marker restructured the block above it. 0.2 has one rule: an open paragraph takes the next nonblank line, and only fence lines, table rows, `***`, a caption under an image or display math, and markers that continue an open list or description list end it without a blank line ([#315](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/315), C2-B-013 to C2-B-020). Only a paragraph takes unindented lines. Every other block continues only on lines indented past its marker, except a fenced block, whose body runs to its closing fence or the end of its container (C2-B-111). A line that repeats a marker, such as `>` or a table row, is read by that marker. A blank line ends every block but a fenced one; after it, only a list item, a description or a footnote goes on, and only with blocks indented to its content (C2-B-009, C2-B-234). Most rows here need one inserted blank line.

## Headings {#headings}

`#` headings read as in 0.1 (U-043). 0.2 also accepts `=` headings, and `carve fmt` writes them; the roadmap ties this to one heading character in prose and in `|=` header cells, with `#` left to tags ([#1092](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/1092)). The remaining rows are tabs, comments and line endings inside a heading line.

**[U-043](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#headings)** <Badge type="info" text="none" /> `#` headings, closing hashes, brace text, seven markers

::: compare no-render
```text
# One
# Two
```
```html
<section id="One">
  <h1>One</h1>
</section>
<section id="Two">
  <h1>Two</h1>
</section>
```
:::

## Thematic breaks and typography {#breaks}

A line of hyphens could be a thematic break, a heading underline or text in 0.1. 0.2 has one break spelling, `***`, so a hyphen run is read by the dash rule alone ([technical rationale](./technical-rationale#reduce-punctuation-collisions), C2-B-159, C2-I-111). Smart quotes follow one opening rule (C2-I-104).

**[U-044](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#breaks)** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Hyphen or underscore run

## Lists and task items {#lists}

0.1 shaped lists with `+` continuation lines, `{loose}`, marker columns and task boxes. In 0.2 blank lines and content columns decide the shape: there is no list continuation marker, and a line past the marker column stays in the item (writer, [rules of 0.1 that become obsolete](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/writer.md#rules-of-01-that-become-obsolete)). The 18 November ruling D1 lets the first marker fix the style of an ordered list ([#6074](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/pull/6074), C2-B-042).

No 0.2 source writes the paragraph bare. The source stays; the tool compares the 0.1 HTML with the <p> added at these paragraphs only and reports each one. A first paragraph with text and no following block image stays bare in both.
:::

## Description lists {#descriptions}

Terms and descriptions own lines by column, like list items. A term follows the continuation rule of every block but the paragraph: after `:: term` only a line indented past the column of the `::` continues it, and an unindented line ends it (C2-B-069, C2-B-076, C2-B-234).

## Tables and captions {#tables}

The GFM separator row mixed the choice of header row with column alignment. In 0.2 every pipe row is a row of cells: header cells start with `|=`, and alignment sits on the cell as `|={<}`, `|={~}` or `|={>}` ([#5091](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/5091), C2-B-171, C2-B-182). A caption line must stand directly below its table or image (C2-B-146).

**[U-055](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#tables)** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> GFM separator row

::: compare no-render
```text
| a | b |
```

## Emphasis and inline marks {#inline}

Bare `_`, `~` and `=` pairs collided with prose and identifiers such as `snake_case`, `~/config` and `x =1, y= 2`. In 0.2 only `/` and `*` pair bare; underline, strike and highlight use the braced forms `{_x_}`, `{~x~}` and `{=x=}` ([technical rationale](./technical-rationale#reduce-punctuation-collisions), C2-I-043, C2-I-046).

**[U-065](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#inline-emphasis-and-typography)** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> In 0.1, `_underlined_` writes an underline, and `_z_/y/` writes an underline followed by literal `/y/`.

```text
an _underlined_ word and snake_case and _id
```
```crv
an {_underlined_} word and snake_case and _id
```

## Escapes {#escapes}

0.2 reads some text as syntax that 0.1 printed as typed: a line that starts with `=`, a letter marker with one space, a shortcut reference with a definition. To keep the 0.1 output, the tool escapes the character that would start the new reading.

::: warning Escapes may still change
The writer escape rules get one data-driven procedure after 0.2.0 ([#6579](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/6579)). The escaped spellings below may change with it.
:::

## Code, math and fences {#code}

```text
<p>a `</p> C2-I-017 reads a backtick run with no closer of its length as text, and so is a `!` or `$` glued before it. 0.1 wrote an empty code span for an empty code value; an adjacent closer joins the opener into a wider run, and a separator changes the empty value. A code, literal-text or math value that starts with a space and a backtick, or ends with a backtick and a space, has no spelling either, since C2-I-016 removes that space (C2-W-077). An empty literal-text run that U-440 cannot remove is reported too: 0.1 wrote nothing for it, and the space before it, which 0.2 drops at the end of the content (C2-I-002), or the empty paragraph or heading it filled has no spelling. Report the parsed range of the run and its value; do not rewrite.
```
:::

## Quotes, divs and admonitions {#containers}

Quotes, divs and line blocks follow the same paragraph and column rules as the top level, so a `+` line no longer joins blocks inside a quote, and a line belongs to the container whose column it reaches. Div labels and titles are read only in their metadata slot (C2-B-119, C2-B-121).

## Attributes {#attributes}

An attribute line applies only to the block on the next line, and an attribute block in running text attaches only to a span, link, image, code span, math, footnote reference, symbol or closed emphasis (C2-B-091, C2-I-036). Attribute text that 0.1 dropped without a trace now stays visible.

## Links, references and definitions {#links}

Definitions stand at column 0 outside quotes and items (C2-B-081), and a duplicate definition no longer replaces the first one. Reference labels may wrap across a line break, so hard-wrapping prose no longer turns a reference into literal brackets ([#1092](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/1092)).

## Footnotes {#footnotes}

A footnote body owns only its indented continuation, so an unindented line after it starts a new block (C2-B-081, C2-B-087). A footnote mark inside link text is written after the link anchor (C2-H-088).

## Comments {#comments}

In 0.1 a `%%` line comment ended at the first closer of its frame, so `[a %% b](/u)` was still a link. The 18 November ruling D2 makes a line comment take every closer on its line, and `%%` directly after the opener of a bracket or braced form is text ([#6074](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/pull/6074), C2-I-023, C2-I-024). Where the HTML check passes, the tool rewrites such a comment as a braced `{% %}` comment.

## Metadata and frontmatter {#metadata}

Line-1 frontmatter reads as in 0.1. New in 0.2.0, a typed `---yaml`, `---toml` or `---json` opener may start an opaque metadata block after line 1, following a blank line or top-level attribute lines; a bare `---` after line 1 stays text ([#6324](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/6324), C2-B-231 to C2-B-233). See [metadata blocks](./metadata-blocks).

**[U-047](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#frontmatter)** <Badge type="info" text="none" /> Format names, the space before them, unclosed frontmatter

::: compare no-render
```text
--- toml
a = 1
---
text
```
```html
<p>text</p>
```
:::

**[U-048](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#frontmatter)** <Badge type="info" text="none" /> Unknown format name

::: compare no-render
```text

a = 1
---
text
```

```html
<p>text</p>
```
:::

## Includes {#includes}

An include directive is a block of its own: there is no inline include, and the line below a directive starts a new block (C2-N-002, C2-B-156). Ids are not renamed across files and footnote labels resolve per file (C2-N-055, C2-N-057).

**[U-011](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#paragraphs-and-blocks)** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> Include directive

::: compare no-render
```text

{{ other.crv }}
```

```html
{{ other.crv }}</p>
```

## Raw HTML and render options {#html}

Raw HTML passthrough was a trusted-content default in 0.1: a host that rendered user input and forgot the flag shipped an XSS hole. In 0.2 `rawHtml` defaults to false, and raw blocks and spans are escaped unless the host opts in ([#2683](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/2683), C2-H-050, C2-H-051). Review every render option instead of reusing a 0.1 options object.

```text
With `social: {mentionUrl: '/u/{user}'}` or `{tagUrl: '/t/{tag}'}` the render is refused with an option error: `{name}` is the only placeholder of a template (C2-H-126), and any other placeholder is refused rather than written into the `href`. 0.1 replaced `{user}` in `mentionUrl` and `{tag}` in `tagUrl` by the name, `<a class="mention" href="/u/alice">`. Write `{name}`.
```
:::

## Extensions and tabs {#extensions}

The 18 November rulings D3 to D7 give extensions explicit source forms such as `:wiki[...]` and `:cite[...]`, and a tabs contract with `selected` and static output, in place of host extensions that read core syntax ([#6070](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/pull/6070)). The extension mechanism is still provisional.

## JavaScript API {#api}

0.2 replaces the one large 0.1 package API with the functions of the `carve-js` package root, and each stage (parse, resolve, render) has its own call.

Move `carveToHtml` callers to `render`, and consumers of old report objects to `renderWithDiagnostics`. `parse` returns a resolved tree, and `parseWithDiagnostics` also returns findings; `render` accepts source or an existing tree. Pass only 0.2 options. Compare site CSS and scripts against the 0.2 section, list and table HTML.

The full replacement table is in [JavaScript API](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#javascript-api); HTML and selector changes are in [HTML and page selectors](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#html-and-page-selectors), and Markdown import in [Markdown import is GFM import](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#markdown-import-is-gfm-import).

## PHP API {#api-php}

0.2 replaces 0.1 in the same Composer package and namespace, `MarkupCarve\Carve`, and the 0.1 classes are gone. The configured `CarveConverter` object gives way to static calls on `MarkupCarve\Carve\Carve` that each take one validated options array.

Move `$converter->convert($source)` to `Carve::render($source, $options)` and keep the options array where you kept the converter. The command line stays `vendor/bin/carve` with the 0.2 commands. The call-by-call table is [Moving a PHP host from Carve 0.1 to 0.2](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve-php/blob/main/docs/migration.md) in carve-php; the summary is in [PHP API](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#php-api).

## Rust API {#api-rust}

The `carve` crate drops its 0.1 engine, and the 0.2 calls live in `carve::api`. The 0.2 `carve` command replaces the 0.1 one.

Move `to_html` to `api::render`, `parse` to `api::parse`, `to_json` to `api::parse` then `api::encode_tree`, and `carve::Options::new()` to `api::Options::default()`. Some calls have no 0.2 counterpart, such as `merge_ast` and `decision_trace`. The call-by-call table is [Migrating from 0.1](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve-rs/blob/main/README.md#migrating-from-01) in the carve-rs README; the summary is in [Rust API](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#rust-api).

## Command line and lint {#cli}

[Tooling](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/tooling.md) specifies the 0.2 commands every engine offers: `render`, `ast`, `fmt`, `lint`, `diagnostics`, `import`, `migrate-ast`, `flatten` and `fix`. The reference engine adds `upgrade`.

Most 0.1 flags keep their names. The ones that move: `--json` and `--ast` become `carve ast`; `migrate --from html` becomes `carve import --from html`, and `migrate --from markdown` becomes `carve import --from gfm`; `--no-raw-html` and `--safe` are the default, and `--raw-html` turns raw HTML on; `fmt --migrate` becomes `carve upgrade --migrate`. The 0.1 `merge` and `trace` commands have no 0.2 replacement: 0.2 has no three-way merge (C2-T-044) and no portable decision trace. `carve lint` exits with 1 only for a warning or an error, so a hint never fails a CI job; `--strict` restores the 0.1 status (C2-T-031, C2-T-051). The full flag table is in [Command line and missing features](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#command-line-and-missing-features).

## The AST 2.0 tree {#ast}

An AST 1.x reader refused any higher minor version, so every schema change was a flag day. AST 2.0 gives every node a must-ignore `data` slot, one node grammar and one reference model, so a later minor stays readable ([#3598](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/issues/3598)).

Stored trees need the 2.0 schema: run `migrateTree` or `carve migrate-ast` before a strict 2.0 decoder reads them, and validate the result. Source spelling moved out of the tree into the [source layout](./ast-source-layout) sidecar. Each row below is a tree change from the [tree and field migration index](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/main/spec/0.2/UPGRADING.md#tree-and-field-migration-index); a field marked dropped does not survive a tree-only migration.

| Row | Change | 0.1 tree | 0.2 tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| T-001 | split | `critic_substitution` with `old` and `new` | a `delete` holding `old`, directly followed by an `insert` holding `new` |
| T-002 | merge | `escaped_text` | `text` with the same `value`, then coalesced with its neighbors |
| T-003 | merge | `cell_wrap` | a `text` node holding one space, then coalesced |
| T-004 | drop | `cellWraps` on `code`, `math` and `raw_inline` | dropped |
| T-005 | move | `rawRef` | dropped; 0.1 references become `collapsed` when `rawRef` ends in `[]` and `full` otherwise; 0.1 has no `shortcut` form; `key` is folded |
| T-006 | merge | `key` on definitions and footnote references | folded |
| T-007 | merge | `attrs.order` and the `keyValues` object | `keyValues` becomes a list of pairs, in the order `attrs.order` gives or else in member order; `order` is dropped; a key named `id` or `class` folds in |
| T-008 | move | an `image` in a list of blocks | a `paragraph` with `role: "image"` that holds the image |
| T-009 | split | a `line_block` with block children | `line` children, split at the breaks of each paragraph, with an empty `line` between stanzas; `lines` is dropped |
| T-010 | move | a heading id in `attrs.id` | kept as an authored id: the draft tree does not say which ids were generated |
| T-011 | move | `marker.bare`, `block_quote.fenced`, `table.sourceFormat` | dropped from the tree; written to a source-layout sidecar when the caller asks for one and supplies the original source, and otherwise dropped |
| T-012 | drop | `definition_list.spacing` | dropped |
| T-013 | drop | the former image promotion stage | dropped; `role: "image"` stays as the tree has it |
| T-014 | drop | the task status `cancelled`, in a draft tree or a 1.2 tree | removed; status derives from the mark |
| T-015 | rename | the former reference spelling field on links and images | `refForm`; the name identifies reference spelling rather than xref display. |
| T-016 | rename | the former cross-reference display field | `display`; the name identifies generated display text rather than reference spelling. |
| T-017 | rename | the former string tooltip field on link reference definitions | `tooltip`; all link target strings use one name, while visible titles stay inline lists. |
| T-018 | merge | the former image and math promotion flags on paragraphs | `role: "image"` and `role: "math"`; one field makes the two exclusive. |
| T-019 | rename | the former camel-case ruby pair node type | `ruby_pair`; the type follows snake_case and carries common node fields. |
| T-020 | rename | the former citation author-suppression flag | `citation.mode: "suppress-author"`; one field determines the mode. |
| T-021 | drop | `citation_group.mode` | removed; every item carries its own mode. |
| T-022 | merge | `citation.locatorLabel` and `citation.locatorValue` | `locator` object with label and inline children; its parts cannot disagree. |
| T-023 | drop | the former stored task state | removed; the state derives from `task.mark`. |
| T-024 | rename | `include.options` string pairs | decoded typed option object; source quoting is written to a source-layout sidecar as optionSpelling when the caller asks for one and supplies the original source, and otherwise dropped. |
| T-025 | drop | `thematic_break.marker`, `table.separatorWidths`, `table_row.continuationLines`, `table_cell.sourceContent`, `strong.boldItalic` | dropped |
| T-026 | move | a definition inside a container | not produced by the draft, which moves it to the document; no change |
| T-027 | move | a named `admonition` whose `kind` is not one of the eight admonition names | a `div` with the name as its first class |
| T-028 | version | 1.x bare document or envelope | document.astVersion = "2.0" and matching envelope.astVersion; reject other major versions |
| T-029 | add | common node fields | optional typed metadata, opaque data, dir, lang and segments; only declared child slots contain nodes |
| T-030 | rename | definition/ref label or abbr | key plus namespace; abbreviation.abbr becomes key |
| T-031 | rename | code_block.content, header and label | value, syntax, title and groupLabel; code_block language is syntax |
| T-032 | rename | frontmatter/raw_block/raw_inline/literal_inline/math content; critic_comment.text | value |
| T-033 | split | comment block, delimited and content | form and value |
| T-034 | merge | list ordered, start, olType, delim, bareMarker, bulletChar; tight | marker object; spacing = tight or loose |
| T-035 | rename | list.items, definition_list.items, table.rows, table_row.cells, citation_group.items | children with typed child slots |
| T-036 | split | table.rows and rowGroups | table_head, table_body, table_foot children, one table_body for each entry of rowGroups.bodies, which keeps its rowHeadColumns and whose headRows rows hold header cells (C2-B-230); table columns move to table_column nodes |
| T-037 | split | table_cell inline children and blocks | cell_paragraph child for inline content; block children for other content |
| T-038 | rename | figure.target and shortCaption | caption.short; the figure itself is unwrapped (T-051, T-052) |
| T-039 | rename | mention.user | target, kind and optional label |
| T-040 | rename | inline_footnote.inline | children |
| T-041 | rename | inline_extension.content | children; declared props, slots, fallback, payload and resourceIds |
| T-042 | rename | heading_ref | xref with key, namespace, href and display |
| T-043 | split | substitution or critic_substitution | delete followed by insert |
| T-044 | add | image alt and target fields | optional decorative, longDescription, targetKind and resourceId |
| T-045 | add | table cell accessibility | optional scope and headerIds |
| T-046 | add | resolution outputs | generatedId, number, resolvedAlign, resolvedValign, href or src, display and table span counts remain in resolved tree |
| T-047 | move | source spelling and physical layout | source-layout record from parseWithLayout; marker, fences, wraps, whitespace and quote choices |
| T-048 | drop | 0.1 rawRef, sourceFormat and layout-only fields | use semantic fields; original spelling is unavailable without source/layout |
| T-049 | add | include directive | include with path, section, typed valid options and the invalid options as written; no expansion in core tree |
| T-050 | add | no extension source record; block extension deferred in an earlier draft | qualified block_extension and inline_extension may carry a typed source record; a block extension has a required core fallback |
| T-051 | merge | a figure that holds one image paragraph, code block, quote or math paragraph, and comments after it | that block, with the caption and the attrs of the figure in its own fields; the comments go where C2-A-082 places them; kind is dropped |
| T-052 | move | any other figure | a figure_group with the same children, caption and attrs; kind is dropped |
| T-053 | move | table_body.headRows | dropped; the groups hold the partition, and the count is written to a source-layout sidecar as headerRows when the caller asks for one and supplies the original source, and otherwise dropped |
